title: Linear First-Order Equations & the Integrating Factor

sections.heading: Section 1: Standard Linear Form and Integrating Factor

questions.q: Write the differential equation $x \frac{dy}{dx} + 2y = 4x^2$ in standard form $\frac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y = Q(x)$ for $x > 0$.
Compute the integrating factor $I(x) = e^{\int P(x) dx}$ for $\frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{2}{x}y = 4x$.
Multiply the standard ODE by $I(x) = x^2$ to solve $\frac{d}{dx}[x^2 y] = 4x^3$.
questions.answer: Integrate: $x^2 y = \int 4x^3 dx = x^4 + C \Rightarrow y = x^2 + \frac{C}{x^2}$.

questions.q: Solve the IVP $\frac{dy}{dx} + y = e^{2x}$ with $y(0) = 1$.
questions.answer: $I(x) = e^x$. $\frac{d}{dx}[e^x y] = e^{3x} \Rightarrow e^x y = \frac{1}{3}e^{3x} + C \Rightarrow y = \frac{1}{3}e^{2x} + C e^{-x}$. Using $y(0) = 1 \Rightarrow 1 = 1/3 + C \Rightarrow C = 2/3$. Thus $y = \frac{1}{3}e^{2x} + \frac{2}{3}e^{-x}$.
This is a homogeneous linear equation with integrating factor $e^{-3x}$: $y = C e^{3x}$. With $y(0) = 4$, $y = 4e^{3x}$.

questions.q: What is the domain of validity for the solution to $x \frac{dy}{dx} + y = 1$ with $y(1) = 2$?
questions.answer: Standard form $\frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{1}{x}y = \frac{1}{x}$ has coefficients discontinuous at $x = 0$. By the Existence and Uniqueness Theorem, the solution through $x_0 = 1 > 0$ exists uniquely on $(0, \infty)$.

questions.q: A tank contains $100\text{ L}$ of water and $10\text{ kg}$ of dissolved salt. Pure water flows in at $3\text{ L/min}$, and the stirred mixture drains at $3\text{ L/min}$. What is the differential equation for the salt amount $A(t)$ in kg?
questions.answer: Rate in $= 0$ (pure water). Rate out $= 3 \times \frac{A}{100} = \frac{3}{100}A$. Differential equation: $\frac{dA}{dt} = -0.03 A$.

questions.q: For the tank above, what is the amount of salt remaining after $t$ minutes?
If salt solution enters at $2\text{ kg/L}$ at a rate of $3\text{ L/min}$, what is the inflow rate of salt in kg/min?
In the solution $y(t) = 5 + 4e^{-2t}$, which part represents the transient response and which represents the steady-state?
questions.answer: Because $\lim_{t \to \infty} 4e^{-2t} = 0$, that term dies out and is called transient; the permanent value $5$ is the steady-state response.

questions.q: What is the time constant $\tau$ for the decaying exponential $e^{-t/\tau} = e^{-5t}$?
After how many time constants ($t = n\tau$) has a decaying transient decayed to less than $1\%$ of its initial value?
questions.answer: At $t = 5\tau$, $e^{-5} \approx 0.0067 < 0.01$ (less than $1\%$ remaining), which is the standard engineering threshold for steady-state.
